Necromancers often use the spell to prepare ground for greater rites, since it marks territory with death’s flavor. The shroud lingers only briefly before dissipating into wisps of darkness. Even once gone, the memory of its suffocating pall tends to linger on its victims.

By intoning words of command, the caster projects their will across the tether between life and death, seizing the strings of an undead creature. The undead briefly stiffens, its will overwhelmed, then turns to obey the caster’s command. Whether skeletal sentry, shambling ghoul, or wandering spirit, the spell asserts dominance and bends the creature to necromantic purpose. At this novice level the control is fragile, lasting only moments, but even a brief shift in loyalty can decide a skirmish. Commanded undead can be redirected to guard an ally, attack their former master, or simply be ordered to freeze in place. The spell is especially feared among enemy necromancers, as it can break their lines of minions in an instant. Failure to maintain the command risks backlash, the creature lashing out in instinctive fury before returning to freedom. With mastery, casters learn to stretch this control further, but even in its briefest form it is a potent battlefield tool. The power whispers of the mastery of lich-kings, who no longer ask but dictate the flow of undeath.

The caster rends open a wound between the mortal world and the spirit realm, allowing a chorus of lost souls to pour through. Their wails echo with sorrow and rage, shaking the courage of all who hear them. The spectral horde swirls in a wide zone, clawing and shrieking at anything living caught within. Enemies stagger, their minds rattled and their movements slowed under the psychic weight of death’s memory. The battlefield becomes a haunted place—shadows stretch unnaturally and every heartbeat feels out of place. Tactically, the spell halts charges and breaks formations, as few can stand steady in the presence of so many dead. Those struck by the wails falter in initiative, losing their tempo. The display lingers briefly, a terrifying wall of sound and presence. When the rift closes, silence falls with a suffocating suddenness.

The caster invokes a curse that seeps directly into the bones of their victim. Flesh blackens around marrow as necrotic energy hollows the skeleton from within. Targets struck feel their limbs weaken, their structure betraying them with sudden fractures or painful weakness. On a battlefield, this spell is a precision strike against heavily armored foes—those who rely on bones and body to carry them through combat. Victims may collapse outright or stagger under the crushing weight of decay. The spell spreads quickly within one target, then echoes outward to a second as rot leaps from bone to bone. This creates panic as enemies see their comrades suddenly falter. Tactically, the spell turns strong frontliners into liabilities, unable to support their own armor. Even after the spell fades, the ache of hollow marrow lingers.

By weaving necrotic force into space itself, the caster seals a chosen area as though it were a tomb. Black iron chains and spectral locks appear from nothing, binding doorways, walls, and even the air itself. Creatures caught inside feel their bodies press downward, as if gravity has doubled, making escape nearly impossible. Those who try to flee find exits sealed by spectral wards, trapping them in an ethereal cage. Tactically, the spell cuts off retreat or confines enemies for destruction. Allies can strike from outside while the trapped foes are forced to endure. The pressure is suffocating, reminding all within that they stand in death’s prison. Once the duration ends, the chains vanish, but many recall the sound of locks clicking shut long after.

The caster raises their arms and draws forth the life of everything caught in their sight. A pall of pale light spreads across the battlefield, dimming flames, wilting leaves, and draining the vigor from flesh. Victims stagger as their vitality seeps away, pulled in threads of ghostly silver toward the caster. Each strand curls into the necromancer’s chest, bolstering their vitality as others weaken. The battlefield becomes eerily quiet, as if the world itself holds its breath while life is stolen. Tactically, this spell serves both offense and sustain, softening enemy ranks while keeping the caster alive. Even mighty champions may falter as their strength is siphoned by invisible hands. Allies feel the drain too if they stray too close, making this a risky but devastating choice. When the spell ends, those who survive are left weakened, trembling at the knowledge their essence was tasted by death.

The caster slams their will into the ground, cracking reality as necrotic force erupts outward. Bones, blackened soil, and spectral fire burst from beneath the battlefield in a tide of ruin. The eruption consumes the area in a storm of shrieking skulls and grave-dust, draining vitality and slowing all caught within. The terrain twists as earth collapses into shallow pits littered with skeletal fraG.O.Dents, turning the battlefield into treacherous ground. Those struck feel their flesh weaken, their speed fail, and their courage shatter. The air hums with a dirge-like resonance, a reminder that death is the only true dominion. Tactically, this spell halts armies, shatters morale, and forces foes into chaos as allies exploit the weakened ground. Survivors crawl from the devastation marked by lingering necrotic burns. Even once the cataclysm fades, the terrain remains scarred, a haunted place that resists healing and growth. The spell is feared not only for its destruction, but for how it reshapes the land itself into a graveyard of its own making.

The necromancer tears open the veil of death itself, birthing a blackened sun that hangs in the sky above the battlefield. This orb radiates necrotic energy in pulsating waves, its light not illumination but a suffocating shadow that extinguishes all warmth. The living feel their life-force wither as their flesh cracks and bones ache under its gaze. Corpses on the field stir, skeletal hands and half-rotted forms rising as the sun’s pulse animates the dead in grotesque parody of life. The terrain warps into a blighted wasteland, flowers withering, rivers slowing, and air thickening with death’s rot. Even spirits are caught, dragged screaming toward the orb, where they circle in endless orbit as a crown of wailing souls. Tactically, the spell halts entire armies: the living are weakened, the dead rise, and morale collapses under the crushing aura. When the black sun fades, nothing remains untouched—soil stays barren, survivors suffer lingering decay, and the memory of the sun’s shadow becomes legend. This is not merely a spell, but an apocalypse contained within a single will.

Divination reveals what is hidden—past, future, truth, or lie. It sharpens intuition, enhances perception, and peels back the veil. This magic doesn’t guarantee answers—it opens the door to seeing them.

A faint shimmer overlays the caster’s vision as veils peel away from sight. Small hidden objects, concealed markings, or faint traces of magic are revealed briefly. The spell does not grant deep insight, but it’s enough to uncover traps, notice hidden compartments, or detect if magic lingers on an object.

The caster closes their eyes and whispers the target’s name. A brief, intuitive flash points toward the target’s last known direction within short range. The vision is momentary—just enough to set the pursuit in motion.

A soft hum fills the caster’s mind as words spoken around them clarify. The spell briefly translates unfamiliar languages into a faint, intuitive understanding. Syntax remains broken, but intent and meaning become clear for a fleeting moment.

The caster’s eyes glow with pale silver light as illusions and lies falter. Within a short radius, hidden doors, concealed glyphs, and invisible entities are outlined faintly. Allies in the area also gain a brief bonus to their perception, making it harder for foes to hide.

Whispering softly, the caster glimpses the threads of probability. For the next few moments, they foresee enemy intentions and ally actions. Allies react faster while enemies hesitate as golden filaments tug at choices not yet made.

The caster tunes their senses to lingering echoes. Within a small radius centered on themselves, faint whispers of recent conversations or presences can be heard. This spectral resonance also reveals the strongest emotion that clung to the space.

The caster’s pupils glaze to mirrored glass as a silent, invisible sensor blossoms at a distant point in space. A faint, rippling bead of distortion forms a 10‑foot sphere, relaying clear sight and muffled sound back to the caster’s senses. Subtle glyph-threads tether the sensor to the caster, steadying the view even as the world turns around it. Veils thin: invisibility silhouettes as pale outlines, and lingering auras stain the air with color. The sensor can be planted in advance and released on a cue, ideal for ambushes or surveillance. Though distant, its presence is slightly concealed, like heat-haze on stone. The caster feels a whisper of wind and the grain of surfaces as if fingertips brushed them. Enemies appear slightly desaturated, making motion easier to track. The effect lasts briefly, but a skilled diviner chains placements to maintain coverage. Used well, it turns any battlefield into a watched board.

A thread of cold understanding darts from the caster’s gaze and stitches itself into chosen foes. Their postures give away timing; armor gaps seem to widen; breath hitches just before they move. Pale sigils float over joints, seams, clasps, and blind‑angles—visible to allies as brief glints. The caster names a target’s weakness, and the party’s strikes fall truer. Each casting churns probability, turning hesitation into certainty. Even guarded foes feel watched, and the pressure slows their hands. For a fleeting exchange, every ally sees what the diviner sees. When the marks fade, the memory of angles lingers a heartbeat longer.

The caster inhales futures and exhales a correction. In the instant before a blow lands, allies flicker along the lines of possibility and reappear a pace aside. Footfalls land where strikes are not; spears find only air as echoes of the allies remain behind. The diviner’s hand cuts three short arcs, mapping safe squares on an unseen grid. A heartbeat of acceleration hums through those moved, a sharpened edge to their timing. The jump is modest but decisive—doorways cleared, traps avoided, flanks seized. Each extra success pulls the path a little farther, as if the future leaned to help. The motion is velvet‑smooth and near‑silent, like thought. For an eyeblink, the world seems to remember two positions at once. Then it chooses the safer one.

With a ripple of silver light, the caster unfolds an immense dome of awareness. Within its boundaries, every secret is dragged into the open: illusions dissolve, concealed foes glow faintly, hidden passages etch themselves into view, and even whispers carry unnaturally clear. The veil does not discriminate—friend and foe alike are laid bare, their weaknesses scrawled across the vision of all who stand inside. The effect is overwhelming, but unmatched for unraveling deception and setting the battlefield in perfect clarity.

The caster’s hands weave luminous filaments of golden thread that lash out to up to five visible targets. Each thread binds into the target’s aura, exposing possible futures. The caster and allies glimpse moments before they occur—attacks before they land, movements before they begin. Targets bound by the threads stagger as their futures rebel against them, suffering slower initiative and faltering strikes. Every ally tied into the weave senses where to step next, as if fate itself whispered the path.

The caster’s form blazes with cascading runes of light, each glyph representing a hidden truth. With a single breath, the veil between what is and what could be tears wide open across the battlefield. All illusions, lies, and concealments collapse instantly; every creature in sight is outlined in blinding clarity, their weaknesses and fates scrawled openly in threads of fire visible to all. For three full rounds, the caster and their allies perceive not only the present but fraG.O.Dents of immediate futures—the swing of a blade before it moves, the crack of a spell before it forms. Enemies reel under the unbearable exposure, their actions faltering as destiny itself resists them. Though awe-inspiring, the Revelation also leaves the caster drained, their mind battered by too many truths at once. This spell is both a blessing and a terror, a force that can end wars—or unmake the diviner in its backlash.
Earth magic calls upon stone, soil, and structure. It grounds movement, reinforces forms, and shapes terrain. This is the magic of endurance, weight, and immovable presence.

The caster flicks their hand and a small pebble rips free from the ground or nearby debris, propelled forward with unnatural force. At its base form, the spell is little more than a magically-guided stone, useful for training, pestering foes, or distracting enemies. Yet, the spell’s simplicity hides its potential: as the practitioner’s mastery deepens, the pebble grows into heavier stones, razor shards, and eventually boulders hurled like meteors.

From beneath the target’s feet, roots and hardened soil surge upward to clutch at their legs. The ground molds into crude, earthen hands that grasp and restrain. Victims find their steps falter, slowed as the soil pulls at their movements. The spell embodies Earth’s protective nature, stopping threats before they reach allies.

The caster calls the essence of stone into their body, forming a skin of hardened earth across their flesh. The rocky coating muffles blows and dulls blades, giving the caster resilience in combat. While heavy, it protects against the most immediate strikes, buying precious time to act. Apprentices use this spell to learn Earth’s duality as both shield and weapon.

With a sharp gesture, jagged spikes of stone erupt from the ground in a sudden and violent display. The eruption pierces upward, skewering anything caught in its line of effect. The terrain itself becomes hazardous, slowing or discouraging enemies who might try to cross. This spell exemplifies the Earth sphere’s ability to weaponize the ground beneath their feet.

The ground itself stirs as the caster commands the earth to rise like a living hand. Jagged roots or rough stone fingers burst upward, clutching the target tightly. The victim finds themselves pinned in place, struggling against the raw weight of the earth. This spell highlights the Earth sphere’s ability to control both terrain and movement through natural force.

The caster draws upon the surrounding earth, shaping it into a protective shell of stone that clings tightly to their form. Jagged shards, hardened plates, and compacted dust fuse into armor, granting a formidable bulwark against attacks. Though heavy and restrictive, the armor greatly reduces harm and makes the caster appear as an immovable force upon the battlefield. This spell embodies the enduring resilience and patience of the earth.

With a crushing roar, the ground beneath the target heaves violently upward, forming a jagged stone spire that erupts from the earth. The sudden upheaval impales or crushes anything caught above it, while also altering the terrain to create a natural barrier. The battlefield shifts dramatically as the earth itself rebels against intruders, leaving both tactical cover and a lasting scar in the land.

The ground churns and splits as massive stone hands burst upward, seizing their target with crushing force. The grip is unyielding, locking the victim in place while jagged rocks tighten around them. This spell embodies the implacable will of the earth—unyielding, unrelenting, and impossible to ignore. Those caught in its grasp find themselves at the mercy of stone itself.

The caster slams their staff or fists into the ground, unleashing a violent surge of stone and shale. The terrain erupts into spinning shards, creating a deadly whirlwind of jagged rock that tears through all within its reach. The battlefield becomes a grinding storm of stone, turning stable ground into a death trap. Such violent upheaval embodies earth’s raw fury, combining natural might with destructive will.

The caster calls upon the primal might of the earth, tearing the battlefield apart with a sudden fissure. The ground splits open violently, swallowing enemies, toppling structures, and leaving behind a scar of devastation. The spell embodies the sheer destructive and uncontrollable power of tectonic upheaval, turning stability into chaos.

The caster commands a mountainside or conjures an overwhelming surge of rock and debris. A massive wall of stone and snow crashes down, crushing enemies and reshaping the battlefield. This spell demonstrates earth’s power not just to defend but to utterly overwhelm, burying foes in a tide of destruction.

The caster draws upon the primal core of the earth, summoning an immense fortress of stone and living rock from beneath the battlefield. The terrain buckles upward as massive walls, towers, and barriers erupt into being, reshaping the battlefield into an impregnable bastion. This is not mere protection—it is domination of the land itself, bending stone to the caster’s indomitable will.

Enchantment alters properties of items, imbuing them with effects temporary or lasting. It’s the subtle reinforcement of armor, the glow in a blade, or the whisper of warmth in a cloak. Magic locked into matter.

The caster channels raw arcane resonance into a chosen item, weaving patterns of light and resonance that cling to its form. At Apprentice level, the effect is simple—an item glows faintly, radiates warmth, or carries a subtle sense of magical presence, marking it as touched by arcane hands. At Novice level, these enchantments sharpen into functional enhancements: a blade that bites harder, a shield that soaks more impact, or a trinket that glimmers with utility. By the time the caster reaches Mastery, multiple items may be empowered at once or layered with several minor effects, each enchantment persisting longer in the fray. At High Mastery, the caster can create battlefield relics whose power lasts beyond combat, resonating for a day or more, their presence shifting the tide of encounters. At Grand Mastery, the enchanter crafts overwhelming temporary artifacts—items burning with multiple enchantments at once, operating at the peak of mortal magic but still destined to fade when their woven resonance unravels. The spell’s beauty lies not in permanence but in the mastery of shaping fleeting brilliance into power.

The caster focuses their will into an object, purging dust, grime, spiritual residue, and unstable arcane traces that linger within it. At first, this manifests as a faint shimmer across the surface, like dew evaporating in dawnlight, leaving the object visually pristine. Beyond the physical, faint distortions of corrupted mana or lingering magical interference are dissolved, creating a stable lattice ready for new enchantments. This spell is indispensable for enchanters who wish to lay a flawless foundation before attempting more complex work, for even the smallest impurity can cause later enchantments to falter or backfire. While it bears little direct combat use, Cleanse is a ritual of care, discipline, and foresight. Its role is subtle yet essential: ensuring that what is built upon the object will endure.

With a touch and a whispered word, the caster causes an object to radiate with soft brilliance. At its simplest, the spell produces a steady glow bright enough to light a dark chamber or guide allies through shadowed halls. The enchantment is more than simple illumination: blades may shine with a polished gleam, armor may shimmer with a lustrous sheen, or jewelry may radiate a subtle aura of charm. Though temporary, the effect makes the object appear more alluring, impressive, or mystical. This small spark of artistry demonstrates enchantment’s role beyond combat, blending beauty and function into everyday tools.

The caster traces a glowing sigil across a surface or object, imbuing it with protective resonance. When triggered, the rune flares with light and creates a brief warding field, shielding the bearer or area from harm. At its simplest, Runeward hardens an object or bolsters a shield with resilience, but clever enchanters etch it on walls, doors, or even clothing for versatile defense. The ward fades quickly after activation, its strength spent, leaving only faint ash-like residue where the rune once glowed.

The caster lays a hand upon a weapon, causing it to hum with energy. For a short time, each strike resonates with a chosen element—flame, frost, lightning, or raw arcane force. Sparks trail from its edge or tip as it moves, making the weapon feel alive in the wielder’s grasp. While temporary, this enhancement can turn even a common blade into a potent tool of battle, glowing with dangerous promise. When the effect fades, the weapon reverts to mundane steel, the resonance discharged.

By pressing their hand to an object, the caster leaves behind a faint shimmering sigil. This mark resonates with the caster’s mana, allowing them to detect or recall the object from a short distance. Adventurers often use Echo Seal to track stolen gear, mark hidden caches, or coordinate with allies through subtle signs. To those attuned, the mark glimmers faintly, like a heartbeat of light pulsing through the material. While temporary, it provides a valuable way to maintain awareness and control over objects across the battlefield or in exploration.

The caster channels steady waves of mana into a chosen item, saturating it with a stable mystical aura. The object vibrates faintly, glowing with soft resonance as its lattice aligns to receive further enchantments. Unlike fleeting buffs or battle-spells, this attunement lingers long after combat, unlocking the object’s capacity to bear complex magical bindings. Attune Item represents a rite of passage for all enchanters who pursue permanence: the moment when an ordinary tool becomes a vessel for lasting power. To observers, the object radiates potential, as though waiting for the next inscription or binding ritual to complete its transformation. While Attune Item carries no combat advantage on its own, it is indispensable in the progression toward artifact creation.

The caster presses two fingers to a weapon’s spine or grip and sketches a swift rune that flares, then settles into a steady ember-glow. A faint hum builds in the metal (or haft), as if the tool were breathing in time with the caster’s pulse. When swung or loosed, the weapon sheds threadlike sparks that trail each motion and vanish as they meet flesh, wood, or stone. The sigil does not sharpen steel; it weaves a temporary strike-channel that converts motion into raw resonant harm. Fighters feel the rhythm immediately—hits land heavier, parries bite, and even glancing blows carry weight. The effect is focused and short-lived, ideal for decisive pushes or finishing strikes. Smiths call it “borrowed edge,” a reminder that true sharpness returns to the mundane when the glow fades. Observers see only a disciplined flare, not a gaudy blaze; this is craftsmanship, not spectacle. When the sigil collapses, the weapon cools in a heartbeat, leaving no mark but memory.

The caster lays a palm on a shield rim, breastplate ridge, or layered leathers, tracing a compact ward-knot that sinks beneath the surface and steadies the wearer’s stance. A subtle pressure surrounds the bearer, like a firm wind always pushing from the right direction. Blows land duller; edges hesitate; impacts disperse across a web of unseen lines. The armor does not thicken—its resonance learns to catch force and pass it sideways. Veterans recognize the feeling: a quiet confidence that turns panic into poise. The sigil shines only when struck, a brief hexagonal shimmer that snaps out as quickly as it appears. For a short window, the wearer stands like a wall, and the wall remembers how to stand. As the rune unwinds, the armor exhales, returning wholly to its natural weight.

The enchanter places a steadying hand on a prepared item while tracing a tight weave of runes in the air. The existing enchantment’s pulse is caught and held, then stitched from “active spell” into “native property.” A soft pressure hush spreads, and the room’s motion feels slightly slowed as the rite aligns. Minute filigree lines appear and sink beneath the surface, leaving only a faint watermark to trained eyes. The process is focused rather than flashy, and most casters perform it outside battle. Its tactical value lies in removing upkeep—turning a time-limited boon into a constant feature of the item. On success, the bound effect no longer counts as a running spell; it is part of the object. The result resists ordinary dispels and endures as long as the item endures. Those who treat this step like a flourish often fail; those who respect pacing leave works that outlast their age.

The caster sketches a circle in the air and snaps it downward; a pale ring blossoms on the ground, then rises as a faint dome. Within the field, allied weapons thrum with a hard, bright resonance that rides each swing and shot. Edges seem to catch the air a fraction longer; strings and bow-limbs settle into perfect line; hafts feel weightless at the instant of impact. The field does not scorch or dazzle—its craft is quiet power, turning trained motion into decisive harm. Enemies sense the difference as glancing blows start to bite and clean hits drive deeper. The perimeter holds steady, its surface resisting intrusion like taut silk, keeping the enchantment’s pattern from fraying under chaos. Commanders time charges to the field’s rise, pouring strength through a narrow window. When the dome fades, the light goes with it, leaving steel honest again. Smiths say it is the sound of a workshop’s best day, trapped for a moment on a battlefield.

The caster traces a seven-stroke rune along a weapon’s line—pommel to tip, grip to head—each stroke flaring, then sinking as if drawn into a hidden vein. The weapon answers with a low, steady tone that riders feel in bone and tendon. On the next breath it moves like a memory you never earned: weight perfectly placed, angle already found, follow-through already true. Every impact plants a bright echo that shivers the target’s guard, while the weapon itself drinks chaos and returns clarity. A secondary mark knots beneath the guard as a silent oath, ready to burst once against hostile magic that tries to seize the wielder or smother the strike. The air around the weapon seems fractionally thicker, as if the world agrees to carry the arc a little farther. This is not permanence; it is ascension on loan—enough to decide a duel, break a line, or write a legend for a day. When the sigil unwinds, the tone fades to silence and the weapon is only what it truly is, though the hand that held it remembers.
Fire magic is raw power—heat, combustion, and destruction. It consumes, clears, and transforms. Practitioners learn to wield not just flame, but the hunger and momentum that fire brings.

A small but potent dart of fire kindles at the caster’s fingertips. With a flick, it darts toward a nearby foe, scorching them with searing flame. While simple at first, this spell is designed to evolve with the caster’s growing mastery, steadily transforming from a modest spark into a devastating barrage of fiery bolts.

A flick of the caster’s hand sends a tiny ember darting forward, glowing with a bright orange spark. Upon striking its target, it bursts with a sharp sting of heat that sears exposed flesh or ignites loose cloth. While the damage is minimal, its reliability makes it a favorite among students learning control of flame. Outside combat, it is often used to light candles, torches, or even kindling.

The caster pulls warmth from the air and bends it into a thin shimmering veil that surrounds their body. This protective field softens the bite of fire, dampening flames that would otherwise sear flesh. Though temporary, it provides a moment of resilience in the heat of battle, allowing the caster to endure sudden bursts of flame. Beyond combat, the technique is sometimes used to withstand brief exposure to harsh environments such as volcanic vents or furnace rooms.

The caster focuses raw fire into a concentrated beam of searing heat that streaks across the battlefield. The ray strikes with precision, burning through armor and igniting whatever it touches. It is more potent than an ember or dart, able to cause real harm in combat, yet it still retains the speed of a direct strike. Outside of combat, the ray is often employed as a tool for cauterizing wounds or smelting small bits of ore, showcasing the utility of controlled flame.

With a forceful gesture, the caster draws flame from the ground or air, shaping it into a blazing barrier. The wall crackles and roars, blocking passage and punishing those who attempt to cross through. While short-lived at Novice mastery, it provides both offense and defense, forcing enemies to choose between delay or injury. Many practitioners use it as a means of herding foes or controlling the flow of battle.

The caster snaps their hand or stomps the ground, causing a sudden burst of embers to flare outward. The cinders scorch lightly but can catch clothing, hair, or dry terrain on fire, creating momentary chaos. Though not devastating in raw damage, it is effective at disrupting groups of enemies or flushing out those in hiding. Practitioners often use this as a warning flare, a combat opener, or a flashy way to make a point in tense negotiations.

The caster thrusts both arms outward, summoning a sweeping tide of flame that races across the battlefield. The wave engulfs everything in its path, scorching earth, armor, and flesh alike while leaving a smoldering trail. Few defensive lines hold against its raw force, and even survivors are often left reeling in smoke and embers. Beyond combat, this spell has been used to clear forests, demolish buildings, and intimidate entire crowds at once.

The caster slams their staff, fist, or foot into the ground, splitting it with a booming crack. A geyser of molten flame bursts upward, then rains down in chunks of blazing rock and searing sparks. The impact leaves craters and fire patches scattered across the battlefield, reshaping the terrain with raw destructive force. Many consider Pyroclasm the signature mark of a true battle-mage, equal parts spectacle and devastation.

The caster’s body ignites in radiant fire as they hurl themselves skyward, exploding outward in a blaze that takes the form of fiery wings. The flames crash down in a wide burst, incinerating enemies while leaving the caster briefly shrouded in heat and light. This spell is often viewed as both a weapon and a statement — the mark of Fire’s rebirth and ferocity. In myth, Phoenix Surge is sometimes said to channel a fraG.O.Dent of elemental spirit through the caster.

The caster rends the sky itself, conjuring a boiling storm of fire and ash. Columns of flame fall randomly within the targeted zone, while the heat bends air and movement falters. The crucible both burns and restrains, forcing enemies to fight against searing gales as the ground cracks beneath them. More than raw destruction, it is imprisonment by living fire, and few can endure its duration.

The caster manifests a spiraling vortex of fire and superheated wind that pulls everything toward its center. The flames whip around like a tornado, reducing visibility and making movement nearly impossible. Enemies are battered by fire damage each round and dragged into the core, where heat and pressure intensify. The spell turns the battlefield into a lethal furnace, consuming terrain and opponents alike.

The caster rends open the firmament, merging earth, air, and sky into a living apocalypse of fire. A colossal inferno sphere manifests, filling the battlefield with flame and heat so intense it warps the land itself. Within the inferno, space bends unnaturally—time slows, movements stutter, and those caught are dragged helplessly by currents of searing wind. Outside the core, flaming chains lash outward, binding and dragging enemies into the furnace. No battlefield, forest, or city can withstand its fury; it is a spell of endings.

Illusion magic crafts what isn’t there—light, sound, shape, and shadow. It doesn’t force belief, but tempts the senses to accept falsehood. This sphere is the art of deception, disguise, and distraction.

A simple illusion of sound or light, Phantom Flicker distracts a single target with a false noise, glimmer, or flicker in their peripheral vision. The effect is fleeting but effective, buying a crucial moment for allies. On the battlefield, it can spoil an enemy’s aim or force them to glance away at the wrong time. Beyond combat, it serves as a tool of trickery for espionage or escape, misdirecting guards or onlookers. Its strength lies in subtlety rather than grandeur, but in the right hands it can shift the course of a skirmish.

Veiled Step cloaks the caster in faint shadows, their outline bending as if wrapped in heat haze. For a brief moment, their presence becomes harder to track, making it useful for repositioning or slipping from an enemy’s gaze. The effect is subtle, not true invisibility, but it can tilt the odds in stealth or combat. In the lore of Illusion, this spell is the first step toward merging with shadows themselves, a glimpse of the deeper shadowmancy to come.

False Face allows the caster to briefly alter their appearance—shifting facial features, changing hair or clothing colors, or masking themselves with a simple disguise. While the illusion will not withstand close physical scrutiny, it is convincing enough at a glance. Adventurers use it to pass as someone else in tense situations, escape notice in a crowd, or hide their true identity. In combat, it can disorient foes for a moment, forcing them to hesitate before striking.

Phantasmal Echoes wraps up to three allies in rippling afterimages that lag a fraction behind each motion. To onlookers, each ally appears to split and rejoin, as if several half-real bodies were occupying the same space. Strikes aimed at one image pass cleanly through while the true form slides aside by inches. The illusions are purely visual but remarkably convincing at combat distance. A trained eye may notice a faint shimmer along edges where light refracts incorrectly, yet chaos often masks the tell. The echoes adapt to stance and footwork, keeping tempo with the bearer’s breath and weight shifts. Archers misjudge gaps, spearmen lunge a hair too soon, and blades carve only light. Outside battle, an escorted group seems larger, bolder, or more formidable than it is. The spell is favored by skirmishers and couriers who must cross contested ground without wearing heavy armor. It is illusion at its most praG.O.Datic: not to terrify, but to make enemies miss.

Specter’s Whisper threads false voices into the minds of up to three creatures within earshot. A guard hears a captain calling from the far corridor; a duelist hears their mentor’s warning at the wrong moment; a mage hears a chant that never began. The sound arrives with directionality and texture, carrying footfalls, breath, or distant clatter as the caster desires. To outside listeners, the air is silent, creating dissonance that unsettles those affected. The whispers cannot force obedience, yet hesitation creeps into timing and judG.O.Dent. A wary target might pause, pivot, or break formation to confirm the ghostly call. In crowded alleys, the effect is devastating, sending patrols chasing echoes. The spell excels at sowing doubt before an ambush or masking an orderly retreat. Subtle casters use it as a scalpel; brash ones as a drumbeat of panic. It is the lie you half-believe because you want to believe it.

Glamour Veil dresses up to three allies in coordinated masks of light and shadow, aligning colors, edges, and silhouettes into a shared deception. With a breath, plain clothes catch moon-sheen, badges bloom on breastplates, and faces assume borrowed dignity. The glamour flows across seams and armor plates, matching the gait and posture the caster imprints. At a distance, the group reads as guards, couriers, or visiting dignitaries; at arm’s length, small tells remain for the attentive. The veil also blurs micro-movements, lending poise and confidence where nerves might betray. In a melee, the same harmonized styling helps allies slip lines and re-form, the enemy’s eyes sliding off their true positions. Street crews use it for quick jobs; agents for exit plans when a room turns cold. The spell rewards planning: choose a role, hold formation, speak like you belong. When belief and illusion meet halfway, doors open.

A tide of shimmering figures surges onto the battlefield, indistinguishable from real soldiers. Their armor clinks, weapons gleam, and voices shout war-cries. Enemies struggle to tell friend from foe, often wasting attacks or retreating under the pressure of numbers. While the illusions cause no direct harm, the confusion they sow can collapse formations and turn morale against itself.

The caster blurs into shadow, creating afterimages with every movement. To enemies, it appears they are in several places at once. Attacks strike empty air, while the caster glides across the battlefield unseen. Though not true teleportation, the trickery is enough to dodge blows and reposition with ease.

With a sweeping gesture, the caster conjures a labyrinth of reflective walls, bending light into impossible corridors. Enemies are trapped inside shifting passages, seeing countless false versions of themselves and their foes. The maze is disorienting, often leading to hesitation, failed strikes, or even allies striking at phantoms.

With a wave, the battlefield fractures into a false ruin: collapsing towers, broken streets, phantom screams of unseen citizens. Enemies stumble through rubble that is not there, ducking falling stones that never land. The illusion engulfs a wide zone, overwhelming senses with sights, sounds, and tremors of disaster. Though the destruction is false, those within lose orientation, strike shadows, and retreat from phantom collapse. To allies, it can feel like standing in two realities at once—the present battlefield and a city’s last moments frozen in nightmare.

The caster tears open the veil between thought and shadow, unleashing a stampede of phantasmal beasts that stalk enemies with terrifying realism. Wolves of smoke, serpents of shadow, and chimera stitched from memory surge through the battlefield. Their howls, roars, and jaws are all illusions, yet the mind makes them real enough to paralyze. Enemies swat at monsters that pass through steel, but fear roots them in place. The zone becomes a hunting ground of nightmares, with every corner another predator’s lair. For allies, the field is chaos but survivable—they can recognize the beasts for what they are if guided. This spell embodies Illusion at its peak: terror as a weapon.

Reality itself bends under Eclipse of Truth as the caster layers sight, sound, and sensation into a single overwhelming deception. The battlefield is swallowed by darkness as a false eclipse rises overhead; shadows twist into predators, terrain folds into labyrinthine corridors, and even the passage of time seems uncertain. Enemies cannot trust their eyes or ears—ally and foe blur together, weapons strike at illusions, and orders dissolve in chaos. Some fall into phantom pits or retreat from collapsing walls that do not exist; others stand paralyzed as shadow beasts circle. For allies, the spell is no less disorienting, though prepared minds can cling to the caster’s guidance. The effect reaches beyond combat: survivors carry doubts of what is real, haunted by lingering visions long after the eclipse fades. At this level, illusion ceases to be trickery—it becomes an alternate truth, imposed on all who behold it.

Life magic nurtures growth, vitality, and biological resilience. It restores wounds, accelerates healing, and stirs dormant energies within the living. It is magic that encourages the body to remember itself.

The caster taps into the raw flow of vitality itself, channeling threads of luminous life-energy into allies. At Apprentice level, this manifests as a simple restorative glow, sealing minor wounds and granting a fleeting warmth of resilience. As Novice, the spell matures into true battlefield healing, knitting flesh while bolstering vigor against toxins. By Master, the Wellspring becomes a font of renewal—its flow able to touch multiple allies, restoring vitality and fortifying their endurance for an entire round. At High Master, the caster not only heals but also shields, weaving protective wards that repel sickness, poisons, and curses while steadily restoring vitality for hours. At Grand Master, the Wellspring blossoms into a radiant beacon of life itself: a resurrection-tier miracle that heals all allies within reach, restores vitality lost to constitution drains, and shields the living with an aura of growth that can even revive the fallen under the G.O.D.’s ruling. This spell showcases the Life sphere’s highest calling—preserving, renewing, and exalting the force of existence itself.

With a gentle gesture, the caster channels a warm pulse of life-energy into a chosen ally. A faint glow spreads from their palm, mending scrapes and easing pain. The warmth lingers briefly, calming nerves and restoring a small measure of strength. In battle, the spell serves as a quick patch to keep allies moving, though its effects fade swiftly after release. Outside of combat, the pulse can ease minor injuries or aches, a comforting reminder of the caster’s bond to the living essence of the world.

The caster willingly shares their own life-force with another, a delicate tether of green-white energy transferring vitality. While it restores an ally’s vigor, the strain leaves the caster weakened, a trade that must be weighed carefully. This spell embodies the raw truth of Life magic: healing often carries cost. The exchange is immediate, the caster feeling their own warmth slip away as their ally rises with newfound strength. It is a tool of sacrifice, a means to keep comrades alive when every heartbeat matters.

A soft hum builds in the caster’s chest before spilling outward as pale-green light, rippling like water across the ground. The wave carries the scent of rain and new leaves, calming hearts and steadying breath. Tiny cuts knit, bruises lighten, and the sting of battle dulls in an instant. Companions feel a shared lift—enough to keep formation, reload, or press an advantage without breaking stride. The magic is precise rather than overwhelming, meant for skirmishes and quick recoveries. It favors coordination: staying close allows the group to catch the same pulse and rise together. Though its glow fades quickly, the aftermath lingers in morale and focus. Veterans learn to move into the caster’s radius at the right moment, treating this wave as a timing tool rather than a cure-all. In quiet, the same ripple can soothe frightened villagers or steady a wounded animal long enough for proper care. Life’s intent here is simple: a communal breath, then back to the work of living.

A slender thread of living light coils around the target’s wrist, then unfurls into a thin, luminous shell. The shell tastes of mint and iron on the tongue, a telltale sign that foreign agents are being pushed out. Black veins lighten, bile settles, and a fever’s heat breaks with a soft hiss. The aegis focuses on purging a present affliction rather than fortifying endlessly. Once the impurity is canceled, a faint strength lingers—just enough to keep the body vigilant until the next exchange of blows. Fighters learn to time the touch between strikes, letting the shell snap into place and burn a toxin out before it spreads. Healers favor it in plague-wards and snakebite country alike, where speed beats ceremony. While the light lasts only a short while, its comfort steadies minds and restores discipline. The spell is not a panacea; some curses and eldritch blights resist mere life-light. Even so, when applied swiftly, it divides the living from the dying.

The caster presses a palm to the earth and feeds it a draught of raw vitality. Soil thickens, roots surge, and green shoots spear upward in a sudden hush. Vines loll across stone, softening hard cover and breaking harsh lines of sight into a gentle lattice. The ground takes on a living spring, as if the battlefield itself exhaled after a long drought. Archers duck behind fresh fronds; blades catch on pliant stems; feet learn caution where there was only dust. Though the growth appears in an instant, it feels natural, not summoned from nowhere but awakened. The effect is most potent in poor soil, where life yearns for any excuse to return. Commanders use it to sculpt lanes, mark rally points, or give pursuit a moment’s pause. Afterward, the plants remain until torn down, burned, or starved. In this way, the spell turns a moment of magic into a lasting change in terrain.

The caster slams their staff into the ground, and roots explode outward in a glowing spiral, forming a protective circle of living wood and flowers. Within this bastion, allies feel their wounds knit shut and curses unravel as the verdant energy pulses each step. Enemies who attempt to enter or remain inside find themselves tangled by living vines, their movements slowed and restricted by the earth’s embrace. The bastion becomes a fortress of vitality: a place where life surges, poison burns away, and foes are punished for encroaching on sacred ground. The contrast is striking—healing warmth to allies, and choking restraint to enemies. In the midst of battle, this spell turns open ground into a fortress of resilience and control.

Threads of green-silver light lance outward from the caster, linking multiple allies in a glowing web. Each thread pulses with shared energy, allowing damage to bleed across the web and vitality to flow in return. When one ally takes a blow, part of it is suspended, delayed in a shimmering ripple of time, only to be dispersed safely later among the group. Meanwhile, each heartbeat sends healing pulses through the chain, mending small cuts and bruises. The battlefield impact is immense: groups bound by this spell become harder to break, their strength pooled across the bond. Yet the link is perilous; if one falls, backlash ripples out, punishing the others. The sight of glowing life-threads weaving allies together is both beautiful and terrifying, reminding foes that the group stands—or falls—as one.

When the caster kneels and thrusts hands into the earth, a surge of raw vitality bursts forth. Grasses, vines, and saplings erupt from barren ground, covering the battlefield in living green. Enemies caught in the growth find roots and branches snaring their limbs, pulling them to the earth with relentless force. At the same time, the plants exude rejuvenating energies, mending wounds of nearby allies and giving them renewed strength. The battlefield shifts completely: once-barren land becomes living terrain that shapes combat, offering cover, healing allies, and hindering foes. The smell of rain, soil, and blooming life overwhelms the senses, making it clear that nature has claimed dominion. Even after the magic fades, the plants remain as natural obstacles and proof of the caster’s will.

The caster strikes the ground with their will, and a colossal surge of life erupts outward. Flowers burst into bloom across barren stone, trees sprout where none stood before, and a shimmering emerald light radiates in all directions. Allies within the zone feel their wounds close, poisons unravel, and their spirits fortified with each pulse of vitality. Enemies caught inside find the very growth of nature turning against them—roots seize their ankles, their limbs are slowed, and the aura of life drains their strength. The battlefield itself transforms into a sanctuary and a prison: allies thrive while enemies are ensnared. Even when the magic fades, the greenery remains as a testament to the caster’s dominion.

The caster calls upon the primal rhythm of existence: life, death, and rebirth. A radiant sphere of golden-green light blossoms, filling the battlefield with the sound of heartbeats. Allies feel their wounds close and vitality return, while the bodies of the fallen stir—the spell suspends the finality of death itself. Those slain within the zone are temporarily restored to fighting form, bound by threads of borrowed life force, though the cost echoes through time. Enemies caught in the sphere feel their vitality siphoned away, their essence drawn into the cycle to empower the living. The spectacle is awe-inspiring: warriors rising from death’s edge, foes faltering as their strength is stolen, and the air heavy with the thrum of fate itself. Yet when the cycle ends, the balance demands payment—those revived must stabilize or perish once more.

The caster unleashes the ultimate expression of life’s dominion, a miracle that transcends battle and reshapes reality itself. With a thunderous pulse, the battlefield blossoms into a living biome: towering trees erupt from stone, rivers of green light course through the ground, and the air fills with the scent of bloom and rebirth. Within this sanctum, allies feel their wounds knit closed instantly, their spirits bolstered, and even the dead rise once more, pulled back into the cycle. Enemies, however, feel their vitality stolen, their limbs bound by vines, and their senses drowned beneath the overwhelming weight of life’s surge. Time itself bends within the zone—death is delayed, wounds resist permanence, and the very concept of decay is suspended. When the dominion ends, the terrain remains forever altered: a lush forest born in the span of heartbeats, an eternal reminder of the caster’s mastery.

Negation is the sphere of undoing—canceling spells, disrupting enchantments, and halting magical effects mid-cast. It doesn’t create; it silences. Practitioners become guardians against the uncontrolled.

A sharp gesture scatters sparks of unweaving energy, snuffing out a minor magical effect. The unraveling looks like ink dissolving in water, eating away at the glow of enchantment until it vanishes. This works best on small cantrips, wards, or simple utility spells.

A shimmering ripple passes over an object as the caster studies it. Enchantments reveal themselves as faint runes or colored veils hovering over the surface. The caster gains a sense of whether the magic is beneficial, harmful, or neutral.
The caster traces a quick sigil in the air and snaps their fingers, unraveling a single minor magical effect from a creature or object within reach. The effect gutters out in a shimmer of gray dust.

With a slow exhale, the caster mutes the magical resonance of a creature or object. For a brief moment, its aura flickers and weakens, making detection more difficult and suppressing minor benefits of enchantments. A faint gray haze clings to the target during the effect.

The caster projects a jagged pulse of black-white static at a foe, attempting to rip active magic apart. The energy arcs like cracking glass, snapping through ongoing protections or buffs. If the casting pushes against an unfamiliar weave, the strain can bite back.

The caster kneels and presses a hand over a rune or ward, pulling loose the threads of its power without triggering it. Lines fade like smoke in a draft as sigils collapse into inert marks. The work takes a focused moment, ideal for traps and seals.

The caster slams their hand into the air, and a shimmering lattice of black-silver sigils cages the battlefield. Within this dome, all ongoing magical effects strain as if under pressure; wards sputter, summoned creatures flicker, and enchantments lose their grip. The effect is localized, forcing spellcasters to contend with a hostile zone of unraveling magic.

With a cutting gesture, the caster conjures a polished obsidian mirror of crackling light. The next spell cast against them or an ally is caught, refracted, and hurled back at its originator. The mirror flashes once before shattering, its shards dissolving into motes of light.

The caster inscribes a glowing seal mid-air; once complete, it detonates in a hush that devours all sound and snuffs magical chants. Casters inside the radius find their words vanish, gestures falter, and spellwork collapses into stillness. The silence is oppressive, broken only when the seal fades.

With a thunderous gesture, the caster tears open a roiling sphere of black static and jagged white arcs. Within its boundaries, all spells unravel—wards collapse, enchantments dissolve, conjured creatures falter, and protective barriers shred. The zone devours both ally and enemy magic, leaving raw silence where no spell can persist. The air hums like shattered glass vibrating in place, reality itself groaning under the negation.

The caster spreads both arms, spinning an immense whirl of mirrored shards and black light around themselves. For a short time, hostile spells that strike the maelstrom are caught, refracted, and flung outward in chaotic arcs. Some rebound on their originators, others scatter to random foes, tearing apart order itself. The storm roars with a thousand voices of half-cast spells, until it finally shatters in a cascade of broken energy.

The caster raises both arms and reality itself shudders. Black fractures crack open in the air, bleeding silence that swallows sound, color, and light. Within this vast shroud, all magic is unmade: wards collapse like sandcastles, enchantments are shredded to threads, conjured beings vanish screaming into void, and even ongoing spells of Grand Master tier falter beneath the unraveling weight. The Veil is not mere dispelling—it is *denial of the arcane’s existence*. The shroud spreads outward in a rolling wave of static silence, extinguishing magic wherever it passes. Both allies and enemies are stripped of their arcane power, left bare to steel and will alone. The air tastes of ash and stillness. When the Veil ends, the world does not immediately recover—magic takes minutes, even hours, to return to balance in the area. The spell is legendary, feared, and whispered of as a weapon that can unmake entire battlefields, kingdoms, or worlds if sustained.

Soul magic interacts with the inner essence of living beings. It can strengthen willpower, reveal karmic echoes, or reach into the deepest layers of identity. This is a sacred magic—personal, powerful, and deeply felt.

The caster places a hand upon a creature or object and opens their inner senses. At its most basic, faint echoes of the soul can be felt—warmth, presence, and vitality—hinting at the unseen patterns that bind life to spirit.

A faint halo of motes gathers at the caster’s brow, like dust caught in lamplight, then sinks into the skin with a comforting warmth. A whisper of remembered voices—ancestors, mentors, guardians—threads through the caster’s thoughts and steadies the breath. The world’s clamor softens; edges of panic round off; doubts lose their bite. On the battlefield this presents as poise under pressure: hands stop shaking, the heart stops racing, and grim determination replaces fear. The effect does not force bravery; it clarifies the will so it can choose. Subtle ripples in the soul make it harder for wandering spirits to probe or tag the caster with a quick reading. Tactically, it’s best triggered just before a charge, when enemy fright tricks or possession attempts are expected. It synergizes well with teams that rely on resolve under fire, buying a brief window to act cleanly. Old wardens taught it as a first defense: know yourself, then the enemy. The glow is barely visible unless one looks from the corner of an eye—and then it’s gone.

A silver thread of light unwinds from the caster’s chest to their palm, pulsing with each heartbeat. On touch the filament leaps into the ally like a spark to tinder, and warmth floods bruised flesh and flagging spirit. The caster feels a brief tug—as if missing a step on a stair—then steadies as the transfer finishes. Wounds do not knit theatrically; they simply stop worsening, and color returns to the cheeks. In the scrum this is a swift triage, shoring up a friend who must not fall before the next exchange. Veterans learn to slide a hand along a forearm in passing, gifting strength without breaking stride. The rite is taboo for theft: it cannot rip life from the unwilling, only give freely. It is most efficient when the team rotates guard over the healer, letting quick touches keep the line intact. Soul schools teach it on day one with a simple rule—“Spend what you can stand.” The thread fades like breath on glass the moment the gift is given.

A pale shimmer flits across the caster’s eyes as their perception slips beyond the physical. Every heartbeat in the area becomes a drum, every surge of feeling a ripple against the skin. The caster perceives not thoughts, but emotional signatures—fear tightening like a fist, anger sparking like static, calm flowing like water. On the battlefield this allows instant reading of morale, revealing who is faltering, who is about to lash out, or where hidden malice waits. Outside of combat it can be used to gauge truthfulness or the general atmosphere of a crowd. The effect is not invasive—it is more like hearing the tone of a voice without knowing the words. Mystics describe it as “colors of the heart” bleeding briefly into sight. The air smells faintly of incense when cast, though no smoke burns.

Threads of pale silver light snake from the caster’s hand and lash around the target like ribbons caught in wind. The strands sink beneath the skin with a chill, anchoring the soul to its vessel and denying easy escape. The victim feels a sudden weight, as though an unseen hand is pressing them into place. Their movements drag, will feels tethered, and a sense of exposure creeps in as though the caster’s gaze reaches deeper than flesh. On the battlefield this halts quick retreats, prevents teleportation, or simply slows a foe long enough for allies to strike. The effect is not cruel by design—it was originally taught to prevent wayward spirits from fleeing before rites could be completed. To onlookers, the target appears wrapped in faint glowing threads that fade after a moment.

The caster raises a hand and conjures a ghostly lantern, its flame a cold white glow that reveals far more than light should. Shadows recoil unnaturally; hidden spirits are dragged into pale outline; invisible bindings are traced like spiderwebs in frost. Within the glow, allies feel safer, as if a quiet guardian watches over them. The lantern hovers just above the caster’s shoulder, moving as they move, and hums faintly with the sound of distant bells. On the battlefield it denies concealment tricks, unmasking cloaked foes or spirit-born threats. In social or investigative play it unmasks disguises of the soul, though not mundane masks. The glow fades after the round, leaving only a faint chill.

Spectral chains burst from the caster’s hands, lashing out with an echoing rattle that vibrates in the bones. The chains are not physical—they bind the essence of a foe. When struck, the target feels the weight of entire lifetimes pressing down, dragging them into stillness. Ethereal shackles clamp around limbs and soul alike, glowing faintly with runic script. Onlookers see the victim slow as if time itself is reluctant to carry them forward. The battlefield shifts: one dangerous opponent is suddenly anchored, slowed, and exposed. The spell was first woven by temple guardians to hold possessed vessels until exorcisms could be attempted. Caster feels tugged at the wrists as if the chains are bidirectional, straining spirit against spirit.

The caster calls upon a spectral guardian, a tall shimmering figure that hovers protectively at their side. The guardian’s form is indistinct—some see a knight, others a robed ancestor, others a beast-totem—but its presence radiates unyielding defense. With a sweep of its arm or wing, it deflects incoming strikes; its mere aura dissuades hostile spirits from approaching. The guardian lasts only moments, but in that span it can turn aside a fatal blow or drive back dark entities. When it fades, its last glance carries silent encouragement, like a parent sending their child into the storm. In combat, allies cluster close, trusting the phantom bulwark. The caster, however, feels the weight: summoning a guardian demands opening one’s soul as anchor, leaving them subtly drained once it departs.

The caster’s body flickers like a candle in wind, then splits into two forms—one remaining faintly visible, the other stepping through unseen corridors of soul-space. For an instant the caster feels stretched, like two notes of the same chord vibrating at once. Then, in a blink, they reappear yards away, leaving behind a fading after-image that bursts in a ripple of ghostly static. Onlookers gasp as the caster crosses impossible distance, circumventing barriers or repositioning behind foes. Though swift, it is not effortless: each step through the astral tears at the edges of one’s being, leaving a ghost-ache in marrow and mind. In lore, this spell is the first initiation into true astral travel, teaching soul mages how to slip sideways into realms between moments.

The caster exhales sharply, and the air warps into a spiraling vortex of pale light and shadow. Ethereal tendrils lash outward, seizing spirits and flesh alike, pulling them toward the churning center. Within the maelstrom, voices scream in forgotten tongues; fraG.O.Dents of broken dreams swirl like debris. The zone distorts movement and balance, dragging enemies together while slowing their actions. Allies feel a similar tug but are cushioned by faint wards if within the caster’s favor. Onlookers see the battlefield bend unnaturally, like a whirlpool in water made of ghostlight. This spell is dangerous even to its wielder—losing grip could pull their own soul into the tide.

The caster closes their eyes and breathes out a plume of frost‑white essence. From the mist rise spectral warriors, translucent figures armed with ethereal weapons, their forms flickering like memories of battles long past. They march in silence, forming a phalanx around the caster and their allies. Each strike of the legion chills the spirit of enemies, sapping resolve and body alike. The summoned host is not fully real—they are echoes—but their presence overwhelms foes with fear and pressure, forcing openings for the living to exploit. Allies gain strength and courage from the guardians, fighting harder under the gaze of the ancestral host. When the spell ends, the legion fades into drifting motes, saluting before dissolving into nothing.

The caster’s eyes blacken as their soul flares outward, blotting the battlefield in a twilight dome of stillness. All sound warps into muffled echoes, colors fade to gray, and every creature feels their heartbeat thunder in their ears. Within the eclipse, souls are bared: phantoms of past deeds flicker around bodies, ancestral voices whisper in a dozen tongues, and mortality presses down like a weight. Enemy spirits find their anchors fraying; allies feel spectral hands at their shoulders, steadying them. The caster stands at the center, arms outstretched, threads of light and shadow stretching from their body into every creature in sight. The dome does not simply restrain or reveal—it judges, binding foes in place, bolstering allies, and threatening to pull the very essence of the unworthy into the void. Even when it ends, the battlefield feels hushed, as though the world itself pauses to recover from what it just witnessed.

Summoning calls creatures, spirits, or constructs across space, time, or realms. Whether temporary allies or long-term bindings, it brings the beyond into the present. Summoners must balance force with control.

A ritual of whispered names and a chalk‑marked circle calls forth a minor spirit in the guise of an animal companion. The familiar manifests with flickering eyes and a faint otherworldly hum, obeying simple commands and sharing quiet impressions with its summoner. It can deliver touch‑range spells and scout cautiously, but it is fragile and unwilling to engage in lethal violence unless the G.O.D. rules otherwise. Concentration keeps the bond taut; breaking it releases the spirit in a harmless puff of motes.

The caster slips their hand through a fold in space and retrieves a small object they already own—belt, pouch, or pack—into their palm. The item arrives with a faint shimmer and settles as if it had always been there. Ideal for clutch moments when rummaging would cost too much time.

The caster calls a gentle wisp from a neighboring plane, a palm‑sized mote that hovers at shoulder height and radiates steady light. It thrums softly, circling the caster and bobbing at points of interest with timid curiosity. While harmless, its presence is comforting and useful in darkness, provided the caster maintains focus.

With a guttural call and a trace of planar energy, the caster summons a loyal but simple beast—a wolf, hound, or other medium animal—to fight or carry loads. The beast bursts into being with a shimmer of dust and growls at the caster’s foes. It obeys basic commands, vanishing when the spell ends. This spell shows how Target + Summon + Duration combine for battlefield utility.

The caster stomps the ground and ghostly soldiers march forth, semi-transparent echoes of ancient warriors. They form a loose wall, blocking passage and striking with spectral weapons. Though weak individually, together they harry enemies and shield allies. This demonstrates AoE + Summon + Shape synergy.

The caster reaches through a thin veil and draws an unattended object from afar. A book from a library shelf, a dropped weapon, or even a set of keys can be yanked into the caster’s hands. The air ripples as the object slides across space into the summoner’s grasp. This spell showcases Target + Summon + Spatial flavor.

With a thunderous chant and the rending of unseen veils, a half-dozen spectral warriors march forth in disciplined formation. Each wields a shimmering weapon and shields allies in their ranks. Their arrival echoes with the clash of unseen battlefields. The warband provides a temporary fighting force, able to harry enemies and defend positions. This spell demonstrates how multi-target + Summon + Duration + modifiers showcase scaling armies.

By driving a shard of onyx into the earth, the caster summons forth a towering construct of stone and shadow. The guardian rises, broad-shouldered and immovable, its eyes glowing with runes of protection. This demonstrates Target + Summon Major + Control synergy.

A glyph of glowing runes forms in a wide circle, dragging forth a struggling outsider. The creature claws and roars as glowing chains lash it to the circle’s edge. This demonstrates AoE container + Summon Major + Control + Shape.

Runes lattice the air as rifts crack open. A disciplined cohort marches in—summoned individually—while a concurrent battle‑aura rolls over the field. Allies feel the rhythm and move in unison; enemies stumble and are shoved back by shield‑pressure as the air itself thickens. This build explicitly separates the “army creation” (Target + Multi‑Target + Summon) from the “formation field” (AoE + Buff + Debuff + Spatial + nested Control), so readers can see the modular assembly.

A bi‑CHAomatic ring unfurls and a gate to twin planes yawns wide. Two opposed outsiders are pulled through to clash while a time‑drag bubble locks the battleground. Gravity sways, courage surges in allies, and foes feel their will slow. This layout shows outer Temporal/Spatial anchoring a Spatial zone, with separate Target containers for two major summons, plus a dedicated Control container that immobilizes both.

When this spell is cast, the battlefield itself becomes a convergence of planes. A monumental sigil ring burns into the ground, rising as a three-dimensional cube of glyph-lattices. Within the shimmering walls, armies stride forth: titanic guardians from one plane, spectral attendants from another, and shifting terrain drawn from both. Gravity flexes, the ground reshapes into ridged fortifications, and pact-threads lash every summoned to the caster’s command. Enemies who step into the cube are slowed and staggered by time-drag while allies feel a surge of courage and speed. At the caster’s word, the sigil flares again, banishing a chosen cadre of enemies in chains of light. The construct endures for the duration, undeniable proof that summoning is the art of weaving containers, not just opening doors.

Time & Space magic manipulates flow, position, and perception. It may accelerate or delay actions, fold distances, or create pockets of stillness. This is a delicate sphere—one misstep can echo far beyond the present.

The caster flickers through space in the blink of an eye, stepping up to 15 feet to a visible space. Air ripples where they stood and snaps where they arrive, a faint echo lagging half a heartbeat behind. Perfect for slipping a grab, dodging into cover, or threading through tight terrain without provoking pursuit.

The caster catches a flicker of the immediate future, as though a page from time briefly turned ahead. This allows them to adjust their reaction at the last moment, granting an edge against danger. The glimpse lasts only a heartbeat, fading before it can cause paradox.

With a subtle gesture, the caster tugs at the flow of time around a single target. The victim’s movements feel heavy, their steps dragging as though they wade through water. Though brief, the effect can tip the scales in fast-paced combat.

The caster vanishes in a flicker of warped light and reappears at a chosen spot within 60 ft. Air snaps with displaced sound, and afterimages linger for a heartbeat. Useful for bypassing obstacles, dodging strikes, or slipping through gaps mid-battle.

With a twisting gesture, the caster slows a foe’s time-flow, binding them as if trapped in syrupy air. Their limbs drag, thoughts stumble, and reaction falters. The snare fades after a round, but in that window, allies can strike freely.

The caster tears open a faint ripple in space and chains their foe to it. The target feels an invisible weight, like gravity fixed them in place. They cannot easily flee or be moved, pinned by unseen bonds of distance itself.

The caster collapses their presence into a singular point, reemerging anywhere in the world within the same heartbeat. The transition is silent but marked by a faint smell of ozone and a shimmer like heat waves. Though instantaneous, the journey passes through dangerous void-currents—failed attempts can scatter pieces of the caster across the fabric of reality. This is the iconic “true teleport,” granting unmatched strategic freedom.

With a thunderous pulse, the caster creates a temporal bubble that distorts the speed of all caught within. Allies feel their actions accelerate, blades and spells blurring; enemies slow, staggering as though time is syrup. Within this zone, battles resolve in seconds that stretch like hours.

The caster tears a jagged wound in space, creating a rift of crushing pressure. The distortion drags foes inward, bending light and air around it like a collapsing star. Those trapped near its edge feel bones stretch and weapons twist, while the center threatens annihilation.

The caster rends reality into a stable shimmering archway, connecting two distant points. Through it, armies can march, caravans can pass, and entire cities can exchange goods in moments. The gate is not without peril: void echoes leak around its edge, and improper anchoring risks flinging travelers into the abyss between places. While open, the portal is a glaring beacon of power that distorts air, gravity, and magic around it.

The caster freezes an entire battlefield in a shimmering dome of suspended time. Arrows halt in midair, flames pause as statues of fire, and creatures stand trapped in half-motion. Inside, only the caster (and optionally chosen allies) can still act, moving between frozen foes like phantoms through a painting. When the field collapses, all delayed events complete in an instant.

With a sweeping gesture, the caster folds reality into an endless maze of doors, corridors, and mirrored halls. Space twists into recursive geometry: enemies turn corners and find themselves back where they started, allies are scattered into parallel passages, and entire armies can vanish into the shifting construct. Distances stretch infinitely; even a single step may take hours, while a mile collapses into an arm’s reach. The labyrinth persists as a living paradox until it unravels, often leaving geography scarred and minds fractured. Villages may find themselves displaced miles away, fortresses may be turned inside-out, and those who wandered within may emerge days older or younger, or not at all.
Transmutation alters the inherent nature of things. Lead becomes gold, water becomes gas, weakness becomes strength. This is the magic of change—refined, radical, or reversible.

The caster runs their hand across cracked stone, and the fraG.O.Dents fuse back together with a faint earthen glow. Chips and fractures vanish, leaving the surface restored to functional strength. This spell is often used for quick battlefield repairs or sealing breaches in walls.

By dipping a hand into murky water, the caster draws out impurities which condense into a faint cloud before dissolving. The liquid clears instantly, becoming safe to drink. A classic spell for survivalists and travelers alike.
A small trinket glows with shifting light as the caster wills it larger or smaller. The object changes size temporarily, useful for concealment, smuggling, or convenience.

The caster traces heatless sigils and the worked metal ripples like wax before settling into a new, serviceable form. Bars bend, plates seal, and crude hinges appear in moments. The effect is fast field‑craft, not master smithing; edges dull, tolerances are rough, and intricate mechanisms won’t survive. Sparks dance across the surface as stresses redistribute, then fade when the form locks.

With a firm command, a mundane object swells to twice its size and weight. Shields become bulwarks, ladders bridge gaps, and tools gain brute leverage at the cost of finesse. The transformation glows briefly, then stabilizes for a short time before snapping back to normal.

Stone darkens, slumps, and collapses into heavy mud under the caster’s touch. Walls sag, flagstones bog, and solid cover turns to a sucking mire in an instant. The created mud is mundane and remains unless otherwise altered by the scene.

The caster slams their hands into the ground, forcing stone to surge up and harden into gleaming alloy. The wall hums with metallic resonance, shielding allies and reshaping the battlefield. Sparks and heat flare as mundane rock becomes a transmuted barrier, persisting until destroyed or dissipated.

By binding two objects together, the caster fuses their essences into a hybrid form. A sword merges with a shield to become a cleaving guard; stone melds with wood into rigid planks. The union lasts only briefly, after which both items warp or splinter under the strain.

With a sweeping gesture, the caster alters scale itself. Weapons grow absurdly large or comically small, ladders stretch into bridges, and crates shrink into handheld bundles. The battlefield bends as proportions rebel against natural law.

With a violent roar, the caster rends the battlefield itself. Stone liquefies, soil folds inward, and a jagged pit yawns open. Weapons and armor caught within warp and twist, their integrity failing. The area becomes an unstable zone where earth and matter ripple as if alive, threatening to drag all into the collapse.

The caster draws disparate elements together into a single indestructible form. Stone, wood, iron, and crystal fuse into an everlasting alloy that defies time. Weapons forged in the zone gain mythical hardness; walls reforged cannot be broken by mortal strength. The spell showcases true mastery of matter’s essence, creating material outside normal physics.

At the pinnacle of alchemy, the caster becomes architect of reality itself. The battlefield trembles as stone flows like rivers, metals fuse into new alloys, and forests bloom or petrify in moments. Entire districts can be reshaped—mountains flattened into plains, deserts turned into fertile valleys, rivers redirected in their courses. The spell is not creation ex nihilo, but absolute reconstitution: what exists is rewritten into a new form. The effort shakes both the caster and the land, for such transformations echo beyond the moment of casting.
Transformation reshapes form without altering substance. Flesh turns to fur, limbs become wings, size expands or contracts. It’s the sphere of self-reinvention and adaptive physicality.
Grants subtle webbing between fingers for temporary swim/climb aid. Appears as faint aquatic lineage and fades quickly.
Faint scales ripple over skin, granting momentary resilience. Subtle sheen, effective vs. cuts for one combat step.
Eyes shift to slitted nocturnal form, enhancing low-light sight but impairing bright vision.

Throat splits lightly along the sides with faint frills that filter water. A bubbling inhale in the river becomes oxygen-rich breath. The skin darkens to damp hues while in use. Perfect for short-term underwater scouting or ambush setups.

Skin ripples with shifting piG.O.Dent, echoing the colors of walls, brush, or stone. To the eye the caster melts into their surroundings, though motion may still betray them. The body feels slick, like standing in a shadow that clings.

One of the caster’s arms bulges and shifts, bones elongating, nails sharpening into claws. Strength surges through the altered limb, muscles coiling with animal force. The arm feels alien but powerful.

From the caster’s back burst broad pinions of sinew and feather. Each beat stirs air with heavy gusts, carrying them skyward with instinctive precision. To onlookers, the transformation is awe-striking, a sudden declaration of predatory dominion. In combat it allows flight above walls and foes, changing the battlefield into three dimensions.

Several allies sprout lean muscle and sharp canines, their frames twitching with bestial energy. Their eyes glow with the same primal hue, their unity undeniable. The battlefield feels suddenly crowded with predators hunting as one.

With a guttural word, the foe’s limbs twist inward, their body reshaping against their will. Muscles knot, joints lock, and for a moment they are trapped in a body that betrays them. The effect is grotesque but short-lived, leaving lingering ache when it ends.

Caster’s body tears and reforms, merging aspects of lion, serpent, and eagle into a terrifying hybrid. A mane bristles, scales plate across skin, and taloned wings unfurl with brutal majesty. Every movement is accompanied by a chorus of alien growls and shrieks.
